pages.title: Flight Control
pages.text: Create: Flight Control adds computers that decide how much each thruster should push. You link parts together with a tool gun instead of wiring redstone.

pages.title: Flight Control Tool Gun
pages.text: Select an engine or controller, then right-click the computer to link it. Also links tanks, sensors and seats.

pages.title: Flight Control Computer
pages.text: Allocates thrust to meet the demand of linked controllers. Goggles show how many engines and controllers are active.

pages.title: Smart Attitude Stabilizer
pages.text: Modes: Level, Level plus Heading, and Hold Attitude. Needs shaft stress from below and a linked computer.

pages.title: Altitude Hold Block
pages.text: Holds the current height, a set height, or only lifts when below a minimum. Needs shaft power.

pages.title: Flight Control Terminal
pages.text: Mouse-driven flight with pitch, yaw and auto bank. Bind a seat to it with the tool gun first.

pages.title: Smart Vector Thruster
pages.text: A thruster whose nozzle swings inside a cone to push in the direction the computer asks for.

pages.title: More parts
pages.text: Other parts: Flight HUD Projector, Attitude Display, Navigation Terminal and Profile Builder, couplers for speed and distance, and a Redstone Proxy that lets redstone toggle modes. Fuel tanks link to thrusters within a short range.
